page: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is a shared-core virtual machine instance belonging to the e2 server family. It features 2 vCPUs allocated from a shared physical Intel Xeon core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instruction sets, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX capabilities.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core execution profiles due to the shared-core architecture. In stress-ng single-core CPU testing, the instance achieves a strong score of 2642.19, placing it in the top 25 percent. However, multi-core CPU performance drops to a weak rating of 2642.78, placing it in the bottom 25 percent. Memory performance is consistently constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 6.36 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 4.83 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10 percent. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall into the bottom 10 percent, reflecting the performance limitations of shared resource allocation.

The e2-medium offers a highly cost-efficient profile for workloads with low resource utilization or bursty CPU demands, leveraging its shared-core model to minimize idle resource costs. However, the performance tradeoffs are significant. It exhibits poor throughput in data-intensive tasks, as shown by a static web serving throughput of 0.63 GB/sec and a Passmark database operations score of 884.33, both in the bottom 10 percent. LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model reach 156.45 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 66.82 tokens/sec for text generation. This instance is best suited for lightweight, non-production workloads, basic development environments, small utility scripts, and low-traffic web serving where high memory bandwidth and sustained multi-core performance are not required.

It is equipped with 4.0 GB of RAM, no local storage, and no GPU. While stress-ng single-core testing shows strong performance at 2642.19, multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into the bottom 10% to 25% due to the shared-resource model. Large-block memory read bandwidth is limited to 6.36 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput is 0.63 GB/sec. This resource-constrained profile makes the e2-medium a cost-efficient option for lightweight, non-production tasks. It is best suited for basic development environments, small utility scripts, and low-traffic web serving rather than database operations or data-intensive processing.
